content: The LMAN1 protein, also referred to as ERGIC-53, is a 53 kDa protein encoded by the LMAN1 gene in humans. It is also known as lectin mannose-binding 1. ERGIC-53 (LMAN1) is a type I integral membrane protein that is localized in the intermediate compartment between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the Golgi apparatus, known as the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC). This protein is thought to recycle between these two cellular compartments. ERGIC-53 is a mannose-specific lectin and belongs to a novel family of plant lectin homologs that function within the secretory pathway of animal cells. Mutations in the LMAN1 gene are associated with a coagulation defect. Through positional cloning, the LMAN1 gene was identified as the causative gene for a rare autosomal recessive disorder called combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII. This disorder is characterized by reduced levels of both coagulation factors V and VIII. Another gene, MCFD2, is also implicated in the combined deficiency of factors V and VIII. ERGIC-53 and MCFD2 form a protein complex that acts as a cargo receptor, facilitating the transport of coagulation factors V and VIII from the ER to the ERGIC and subsequently to the Golgi apparatus. Mutational inactivation of LMAN1 is a frequent and early event that may contribute to the development of colorectal cancer.
